config.templates.project.url.description: Repository URL for the default project template (e.g. https://github.com/org/repo.git)
config.templates.project.ref.description: Git ref (branch, tag, or commit) for the project template
config.templates.mod.url.description: Repository URL for the default mod template
config.templates.mod.ref.description: Git ref (branch, tag, or commit) for the mod template
config.templates.workshop.url.descriptio: Repository URL for the default workshop template
config.templates.workshop.ref.descriptio: Git ref (branch, tag, or commit) for the workshop template
config.templates.language.url.descriptio: Repository URL for the default language template
config.templates.language.ref.descriptio: Git ref (branch, tag, or commit) for the language template
config.useSymlinks.description: Use directory junctions instead of copying shared template folders (.libraries, .template-*) when running New Project (--symlinks). Build output is not affected.
config.verbose.description: Enable verbose/diagnostic output for all commands (--verbose)
config.offline.description: Skip remote template refresh and use cached/legacy data (--offline). Applies to New Project and Add Mod.
config.forceUpdate.description: Force refresh of cached templates (--force-update). Applies to New Project and Add Mod.
config.build.target.description: Build target mode. Controls whether to build the main or dev_branch workshop output, or both. A specific target overrides project.json's build.target.
config.build.target.enumDescriptions.def: Build the main workshop output (same as production)
config.build.target.enumDescriptions.bot: Build both the main and the dev_branch workshop outputs (--both).
config.confirmBeforeRun.description: Ask for confirmation before running Build or Clean (protects against misclicks while the game is debugging the output).
config.language.description: Display language for the PZ Studio UI (explorer tree, prompts, and notifications). 'auto' follows the VS Code display language. Command titles and setting descriptions shown by VS Code always follow the VS Code display language.
